displayName: L3 app.constrap.com: HTTPS check failing from two or more locations for 10 minutes

conditions.displayName: Uptime check on app.constrap.com failing from 2+ checker locations for 10 minutes

documentation.subject: app.constrap.com is failing its public HTTPS check
documentation.content:
## What this means Google's uptime checkers request `https://app.constrap.com/` every 5 minutes from several locations. At least two locations have failed for 10 minutes. A check passes only with HTTP 200, a valid TLS certificate, a response within 10 seconds, and the application shell (`
`) in the body. **Likely effect:** users cannot load Constrap, or see a certificate warning. **What a passing check does NOT prove:** that sign-in, Firestore, Storage or the Cloud Functions work. It requests one public static page. ## Check, in this order 1. **Is it real?** From your own machine: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' https://app.constrap.com/` (expect `200`). Open the uptime check in Cloud Monitoring to see which locations fail and with what error. 2. **Billing.** `gcloud billing projects describe constrapp-69b5d` must show `billingEnabled: true`. 3. **Certificate.** `echo | openssl s_client -connect app.constrap.com:443 -servername app.constrap.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate`. An expired or mismatched certificate points at the custom domain: Firebase Console, Hosting, custom domains. 4. **DNS.** `dig +short app.constrap.com` must still resolve to Firebase Hosting. A change at the registrar or DNS host breaks the domain while `https://constrapp-69b5d.web.app/` keeps working: compare the two. 5. **Recent release.** Firebase Console, Hosting, release history. If the failure started at a deploy and the default `web.app` origin fails too, roll back to the previous release in the console (Product Owner approval). 6. **Google status.** https://status.firebase.google.com/ and https://status.cloud.google.com/ for a Hosting incident. ## After recovery The incident closes by itself once the check passes again. Record the start, end, cause and action in the incident log. Runbook: `ops/RUNBOOK.md`.
